title: Issued NHC wind speed probabilities for 592 storms (2008-2025) were too low in the Atlantic and too high in the eastern Pacific against best-track wind radii
abstract: Question: are the public NHC/CPHC Tropical Cyclone Wind Speed Probabilities calibrated? Approach: we parsed all 12,978 archived text products of 2008-2025 (249,386 rows of location, threshold and 12-120 h cumulative probability; 592 storms). The outcome is exposure to the final HURDAT2 quadrant wind radii of the same storm, interpolated in azimuth as in the developer verification. We wrote and hashed the plan before scoring. Confidence intervals resample whole storms. Results: for 0-120 h, observed/expected events were 1.18 (95% CI 1.09-1.27) at 34 kt, 1.28 (1.12-1.42) at 50 kt and 1.10 (0.96-1.23) at 64 kt. Mid-range probabilities occurred about 10 points more often than stated. Pre-specified truth variants move these ratios by about 0.1 (0.85 x radii: 0.99, 1.08, 0.90). The basins had opposite errors under every truth: at 34 kt the ratio was 1.28 (1.16-1.39) in the Atlantic and 0.89 (0.79-0.98) in the eastern and central Pacific. In exploratory matching to official forecast advisories, Pacific ratios fell from about 1.0 within 75 nm of the official track to 0.34 at 200-300 nm, and official Pacific 34-kt radii were 6-19% larger than best-track radii at 24-72 h. Atlantic ratios were 1.30-1.37 within 150 nm of the track, with official radii within 6% of best track; the Atlantic deficit was largest at the coast and in 2020-2025 (1.52). The pre-registered intensity hypothesis was not supported (recalibration slope difference -0.05, CI -0.16 to 0.07). A lagged five-season track-error climatology had weak support (Spearman rho -0.29, one-sided p 0.042). Limitations: best-track radii are uncertain maximum extents; only listed locations (34-kt 120-h probability of 3% or more) are scored; attribution is correlational and the NHC Monte Carlo model was not re-run.

display.caption: Observed/expected events by cumulative forecast period for 34, 50 and 64 kt (592 storms, 2008-2025). Points: primary truth with 95% storm-bootstrap CI. Band: range from 0.85 x interpolated radii to quadrant-step radii.

34-kt, 0-120 h observed/expected events by basin and coast-distance class, and by basin and era. The Atlantic is under-forecast and the eastern Pacific over-forecast under every truth definition (pale bars).

Left: 34-kt observed/expected events by minimum distance of the location from the official forecast track. Right: best-track/official mean 34-kt radius by official lead time. Pacific probabilities are too high far from the track, where official radii were too large.
